title: Ship a home as one pushed git ref to a path on this machine, fetch it into a second home with an arrival beside each session's head, and resume it through the launch template
purpose: Today a home lives only on the machine that captured it. Stage 3 of the context roadmap moves a home as a pushed ref the target fetches, never a hand copy, keeps the source intact, and gives the target a distinct execution id with its ancestry recorded. This brief delivers stage 3's first block, the same-machine proof: `lys-home ship` makes a home a git repository tracking exactly its sessions, index and head files, blocks and templates, and pushes it as one fast-forward ref to a bare repository at a path on this machine (ADR-073); `lys-home fetch` pulls that ref into a new, empty second home, verifies every index, head, block and template strictly, and hangs one arrival event beside each session's head with a fresh execution id of that session's own (ADR-074); and the fetched home is rendered and resumed through the Claude Code launch template on the installed version, written up as a proof of hashes, counts and paths. The ref this brief ships is what the second-machine block will fetch once stage 3's preconditions exist.
task:
Build on the home record (HOME-001), the launch template (HOME-002) and `lys-home given` (HOME-003), which the index_missing and head_missing refusals name as the act that answers them, all on main. New logic goes in new files: `crates/lys-home/src/record/mod.rs` holds 472 of its 500 code lines and `crates/lys-home/src/cli.rs` 433, so each gains only `pub mod` lines, the two enum arms and their dispatch. Work in the order of the requirements: the exact tracked set (R1); a strict verification that never rebuilds an index (R2), because `Index::read` rebuilds a stale index in memory and `Index::load` writes it, so either called from ship or fetch would let a stale index through with every test green; the pinned git runner and the local-path rule (R3); the `arrival` event kind (R4); `ship` (R5); `fetch` (R6); the end-to-end secret search and render check (R7); the documents (R8); the proof (R9).

The ref is fixed: `refs/lys/home`, in the home's own repository and on the remote; no command-line argument names it. The lock file the code keeps beside `sessions/<id>.jsonl` is `sessions/<id>..lock` (a doubled dot, because `Index::lock_path` passes the suffix `.lock` to `sibling`); the tracked set leaves it out by enumeration, not by pattern. `record::take_lock` is private to `record/mod.rs`; a module under `record/` reaches it as `super::take_lock`. Ship takes every session's lock before it reads any session and holds them all until the commit is written, so no seat can append between the check and the snapshot; it releases them before it pushes.

Remotes: in this brief a remote is a path on this machine and nothing else, for ship and for fetch alike. No estate-hosts file, ssh configuration or host list is read or written; every ssh remote, https, git or file URL and hosted service is refused as `remote_not_local`, whose words say that shipping off this machine waits for stage 3's encryption from the secrets step. Stage 3's precondition, encryption before any bytes leave the machine, stands as the context roadmap and the home design's non-goal on moving a home between devices state it, and neither is edited.

Secrets: the card's words say no credential, token or secret value is ever tracked in the home. That sentence is corrected here: no credential lys-home holds is ever written into the home (CN8), and that is the only secret guarantee ship makes. Ship does not scan tracked files for secrets. Blocks hold imported tool results verbatim and a template's env and mcp slots are free strings, so a secret a tool printed or a person typed can be in a home and no scan can promise to find every such value; that is why ship takes only a path on this machine. The fixture acceptance (R7) stays: a use-only secret's value set in the environment of every lys-home process the test runs is found in no object the shipped ref reaches.

The arrival's execution id is `record::fresh_id` (32 lowercase hex digits), one per arriving session; there is no home-level id file. The arrival carries the remote as its absolute path in `detail`, and fetch refuses, before it writes anything, a remote whose arrival data would pass the 512-byte cap. Fetch commits the arrival entries it appends as one commit in the target's repository, whose one parent is the fetched commit and whose message names the source commit, the remote and the ref, so `git status` in the target is clean after fetch and a later ship from the target carries the arrival onward; if the append or the commit fails, fetch removes what it created and refuses as `arrival_failed`. Git runs as the `git` binary on PATH, never a git crate; the gate machine needs `git` on PATH for the integration tests. No test reaches the network: every remote in a test is a path in a temporary directory, and a refused remote is refused before any process starts.

Out of scope: the named second machine (stage 3's second block), read authority over a home, encryption of a home, harnesses other than Claude Code, any transport but a git ref to a path on this machine, and a flag for ship to leave a session out.

requirements.title: Enumerate a home's tracked set exactly
requirements.spec: Add `crates/lys-home/src/record/tracked.rs` with a public function returning a home's tracked set as home-relative paths with `/` separators, sorted in byte order. WHEN the tracked set is taken, THE SYSTEM SHALL return exactly: for each session id `Home::session_ids` lists, `sessions/<id>.jsonl`, `sessions/<id>.index.jsonl` and `sessions/<id>.head` that exist; each file `blocks/<hh>/<name>` whose name is 64 lowercase hex digits and whose directory `<hh>` is the name's first two characters; and each file `templates/<hh>/<name>` by the same rule. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT include a lock file (`sessions/<id>..lock`), a head temporary (`sessions/<id>.head.tmp`), a block temporary (any name beginning with `.` under `blocks/`), any file at the home root, any file under `.git`, or any other file, and SHALL NOT select files by glob pattern or by a `.gitignore` file.
acceptance: A unit test builds a home holding session `fixture` (its `.jsonl`, `.index.jsonl`, `.head` and `fixture..lock`), one block put through `BlockStore::put`, one template put through `TemplateStore::put`, the files `blocks/.incoming.1.00.tmp`, `sessions/fixture.head.tmp` and `notes.txt` at the root, and asserts the tracked set is exactly 5 paths in this order: `blocks/<hh>/<block hash>`, `sessions/fixture.head`, `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl`, `sessions/fixture.jsonl`, `templates/<hh>/<template hash>`.

A file under `blocks/ab/` named by 64 lowercase hex digits that start `cd`, and a file under `blocks/<hh>/` named by a block's hash in uppercase, are both absent from the tracked set, which still has 5 paths.
`grep -n 'glob\|gitignore' crates/lys-home/src/record/tracked.rs` prints nothing.

requirements.title: Verify a home strictly without rebuilding anything
requirements.spec: Add `crates/lys-home/src/record/verify.rs` and a crate-visible strict read in `crates/lys-home/src/record/index.rs` that uses `Index::from_cached` and never falls back to `Index::scan`. WHEN a home is verified, THE SYSTEM SHALL give, for each session in `Home::session_ids` order, at most one reason, the first that applies in this order: `index_missing` when `sessions/<id>.index.jsonl` does not exist; `index_not_this_file` when it exists and a row of it does not parse (where `Index::read_rows` gives `Malformed`), or when its rows are not the session file's by the rule `from_cached` applies; `head_missing` when `sessions/<id>.head` does not exist; `head_not_indexed` when the head file names a non-empty id the index does not hold. WHERE blocks and templates are asked for, THE SYSTEM SHALL name every file of the tracked set under `blocks/` whose bytes do not hash to its name, and likewise under `templates/`, each by its name, in byte order. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT call `Index::read`, `Index::load` or `Index::scan` from `verify.rs`, SHALL NOT write, rename or remove any file, and SHALL NOT put a line, an entry's data or a block's or template's bytes in the result.
acceptance: The fixture home of every line below is built in `verify_tests.rs` in this order: `Home::open` on an empty temporary directory; `crates/lys-home/tests/fixtures/launch/session.jsonl` copied byte for byte to `sessions/fixture.jsonl`; then one `render_launch` (the function behind `render-launch`) of `crates/lys-home/tests/fixtures/launch/template.json` on session `fixture`, with `out` a second empty temporary directory. Before any check runs the test asserts that `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` and `sessions/fixture.head` exist, that `templates/` holds exactly one file (the stored template) and that `blocks/` holds at least one file (the render's manifest block). Verifying that home gives no session reason, no bad block and no bad template.

After one well-formed entry line is appended to `sessions/fixture.jsonl` directly, bypassing the index, verification gives session `fixture` the reason `index_not_this_file`, and the SHA-256 of `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` is the same before and after the verification.
With `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` removed, verification gives `index_missing`, and no index file exists afterwards.
With `sessions/fixture.head` removed, verification gives `head_missing` and no head file exists afterwards; with the head file's bytes replaced by `nope\n`, it gives `head_not_indexed`.

With the bytes of the render's manifest block (the file under `blocks/` named by the `record` hash of the `template_render` event the render appended) replaced by `corrupted-block-bytes`, verification names exactly that block's hash among bad blocks and the result serialised as JSON does not contain `corrupted-block-bytes`; with the bytes of the one stored template under `templates/` replaced the same way, it names exactly that template's hash among bad templates.

With the bytes of `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` replaced by `not json`, verification gives session `fixture` the reason `index_not_this_file`, and the SHA-256 of `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` is the same before and after the verification.
`grep -nE 'Index::(read|load|scan)' crates/lys-home/src/record/verify.rs` prints nothing.

Two drift injections, each recorded in the dev record: making the strict read fall back to `Index::scan` when `from_cached` refuses the rows makes exactly one test fail, the appended-line `index_not_this_file` test; making it fall back to `Index::scan` when `Index::read_rows` gives `Malformed` makes exactly one test fail, the `not json` `index_not_this_file` test.

requirements.title: Run git with a pinned environment and take a remote only when it is a path on this machine
requirements.spec: Add `crates/lys-home/src/home_move/git.rs` and `crates/lys-home/src/home_move/remote.rs`, with `crates/lys-home/src/home_move/mod.rs` carrying only `pub mod` lines and module docs, the module named in `crates/lys-home/src/lib.rs`, and the refusals added to `HomeError` in `crates/lys-home/src/error.rs`. The runner SHALL take the environment it inherits as an explicit argument, which ship and fetch fill from the process environment. WHEN ship or fetch runs a git command, THE SYSTEM SHALL start the `git` binary found on PATH with its environment cleared and only `PATH` kept from that argument, with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` set to the null device, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` set explicitly, author and committer `lys-home <lys-home@invalid>`, and `-c core.autocrlf=false -c core.hooksPath=<null device> -c core.attributesFile=<null device> -c commit.gpgsign=false -c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.file.allow=always`, and SHALL write each file into a repository with `git hash-object -w --no-filters`. IF a git command exits non-zero, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with `git_failed`, naming the git subcommand and its exit code and no output of it. WHEN a remote argument is taken, THE SYSTEM SHALL accept it only when it contains no `://` and no `:` before its first `/`, and SHALL resolve it against a base directory it is given, which ship and fetch fill with the process's current directory, joining the two and making the result absolute with `std::path::absolute`. IF the remote is anything else, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with the error text `remote_not_local: `<remote>` is not a path on this machine; shipping off this machine waits for stage 3's encryption from the secrets step`, before any process starts and before any file is written. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT read ssh configuration, an estate-hosts file or any list of hosts, SHALL NOT start `ssh` or any other network transport, SHALL NOT depend on a git crate, and SHALL NOT add a dependency to any Cargo.toml.
acceptance: Each of `ssh://host.example/r.git`, `host.example:r.git`, `git@github.com:o/r.git`, `https://github.com/o/r.git`, `git://host.example/r.git` and `file:///tmp/r.git` is refused with an error whose text starts `remote_not_local` and contains `shipping off this machine waits for stage 3's encryption from the secrets step`.
`/tmp/r.git` is taken as `/tmp/r.git`; with the base directory `/tmp/work`, `r.git` is taken as `/tmp/work/r.git` and `./a:b` as `/tmp/work/a:b`.

A unit test gives the runner an inherited environment holding `PATH`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` naming a file that sets `user.name = someone` and `core.autocrlf = true`, and `HOME` naming a temporary directory whose `.gitconfig` sets the same two keys, commits a file holding `a
b
` through the runner, and asserts the commit's author is `lys-home <lys-home@invalid>` and the committed blob's bytes are `a
b
`; the test process's own environment and current directory are not changed.
`grep -rnE 'estate-hosts|\.ssh|"ssh"' crates/lys-home/src` prints nothing.
The `[dependencies]` table of `crates/lys-home/Cargo.toml` names exactly clap, rand, serde, serde_json, sha1, sha2, thiserror and time.

requirements.title: Add the arrival event kind
requirements.spec: In `crates/lys-home/src/harness/claude_code/events.rs` add `KIND_ARRIVAL = "arrival"`, the seventh kind, and a constructor taking the source commit, the remote, the ref and the execution id that returns a `HarnessEvent` with `source_uuid` and `record` both `None` and `detail` holding exactly the keys `source_commit`, `remote`, `ref` and `execution`. WHEN the arrival's data is taken, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it through the existing `MAX_DATA_BYTES` check when it exceeds 512 bytes. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT change the six existing kinds, their constants or their data, SHALL NOT change `MAX_DATA_BYTES`, SHALL NOT store a block for an arrival, and SHALL NOT add a field to Pi's grammar: the arrival is a `custom` entry of type `lys.harness_event`.
acceptance: The data of the arrival for source commit `a` repeated 40 times, remote `/r.git`, ref `refs/lys/home` and execution `b` repeated 32 times equals `{"kind":"arrival","harness":"claude-code","source_uuid":null,"record":null,"detail":{"execution":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb","ref":"refs/lys/home","remote":"/r.git","source_commit":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"}}` compared as `serde_json::Value`.
The same arrival with a remote of `/` followed by 399 `x` characters is refused with `HomeError::EventTooLarge`.

`KIND_HOOK`, `KIND_PERMISSION_MODE`, `KIND_TOOL_COMPLETED`, `KIND_ATTACHMENT`, `KIND_SYSTEM` and `KIND_TEMPLATE_RENDER` keep the values `hook`, `permission_mode`, `tool_completed`, `attachment`, `system` and `template_render`, and `MAX_DATA_BYTES` is 512.
Every test in `events_tests.rs` that existed before this brief passes unchanged.

requirements.title: Ship a home as one fast-forward ref to a path on this machine
requirements.spec: Add `lys-home ship --home <dir> --remote <path>`: its arguments and run function in `crates/lys-home/src/cli_move.rs`, its enum arm and dispatch in `crates/lys-home/src/cli.rs`, its logic in `crates/lys-home/src/home_move/ship.rs`, the holding of every session's lock in `crates/lys-home/src/record/hold.rs`, and its refusals as `HomeError` variants whose text begins with the refusal's name and `: `. WHEN ship runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL check, in this order and before writing anything: take the remote (R3); open the home with `Home::read`; IF the home lists no session, THEN refuse with `empty_home: the home at <dir> holds no sessions, so there is nothing a fetch could arrive with; ship after a session has been captured`; IF the remote path exists and is not a bare repository, THEN refuse with `remote_not_bare`, naming the path and what it found, one of `a file`, `a non-bare repository` or `a directory that is not a bare repository`; take every session's lock with the same non-blocking lock `take_lock` takes, without loading an index, and IF any is held by another owner, THEN refuse with `session_held: session `<id>` is held by a live owner; ship after that seat stops`, without waiting; for each session in `Home::session_ids` order, IF its index file does not exist, THEN refuse with `index_missing`, and IF its head file does not exist, THEN refuse with `head_missing`, each naming the session, the missing file as `sessions/<id>.index.jsonl` or `sessions/<id>.head`, and the act `run lys-home given --home <dir> --session <id>, which writes that session's index and head, then ship again`; IF verification (R2, sessions only) gives any session `index_not_this_file` or `head_not_indexed`, THEN print `{"command": "ship", "refused": "stale_index", "sessions": [{"session": <id>, "reason": <reason>}, ...]}` on stdout, one element per such session, and exit 1; IF `<home>/.git` exists and its index or its `refs/lys/home` commit tracks a path outside the tracked set (R1), THEN refuse with `foreign_tracked`, naming each such path in byte order. WHEN every check passes, THE SYSTEM SHALL initialise `<home>/.git` when it does not exist, stage exactly the tracked set, and, IF the staged tree equals the tree of the home repository's `refs/lys/home` commit, THEN make no new commit and take that commit, ELSE commit the tree with that commit as its parent when there is one and update `refs/lys/home` to it; then release every session lock; initialise a bare repository at the remote path when the path does not exist; IF the remote's `refs/lys/home` names a commit that is not the taken commit and is not its ancestor, THEN refuse with `ref_diverged`, naming the ref, the remote's commit and the taken commit, and write nothing to the remote; otherwise push the taken commit to the remote's `refs/lys/home` without force, and print `{"command": "ship", "report": {"commit", "ref", "remote", "initialised", "remote_created", "unchanged", "note"}}`, where `remote` is the absolute remote path, `unchanged` is true exactly when no new commit was made, and `note` is `the home is unchanged since <commit>; no new commit was made` when `unchanged` is true and the empty string otherwise. Every refusal but `stale_index` is printed on stderr with nothing on stdout and exits 1. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT force-push, SHALL NOT scan the tracked files for secrets, SHALL NOT write, rename, truncate or remove any file of the tracked set, SHALL NOT write an index or a head file, SHALL NOT call `Index::load` or `Session::open`, SHALL NOT offer a way to leave a session out, and SHALL NOT put transcript content, an entry's data or a block's bytes in a report or an error.
acceptance: In `tests/home_ship.rs`, run through the binary on a fixture home made from `tests/fixtures/launch/session.jsonl` as session `fixture`, with one `render-launch` of `tests/fixtures/launch/template.json` already run on it: `ship --remote <tmp>/remote.git` with `<tmp>/remote.git` absent exits 0 and reports `initialised` true, `remote_created` true, `unchanged` false, `note` the empty string, `ref` `refs/lys/home`, `remote` the absolute path of `<tmp>/remote.git`, and a `commit` of 40 lowercase hex digits equal to the output of `git --git-dir <tmp>/remote.git rev-parse refs/lys/home`.
`git --git-dir <tmp>/remote.git ls-tree -r --name-only refs/lys/home` prints exactly the fixture home's tracked set (R1), one `templates/` path and at least one `blocks/` path among them.
Shipping to `<tmp>/bare.git` made beforehand with `git init --bare` exits 0 with `remote_created` false, and `git --git-dir <tmp>/bare.git rev-parse refs/lys/home` prints the report's commit.

Shipping to a remote path that is a regular file exits 1 with stderr containing `remote_not_bare`, the path and `a file`; to a directory made by `git init`, with `remote_not_bare` and `a non-bare repository`; to a directory holding one file `x.txt`, with `remote_not_bare` and `a directory that is not a bare repository`; the file's SHA-256 is unchanged in the first case, the directory's listing and file hashes are unchanged in the other two and `<home>/.git` does not exist.

Shipping to `host.example:r.git`, to `ssh://host.example/r.git` and to `https://github.com/o/r.git` each exits 1 with stderr starting `remote_not_local` and containing `shipping off this machine waits for stage 3's encryption from the secrets step`, and the listings of the home and of the current directory are the same before and after.

Shipping a home made by `Home::open` with no session and one block put through `BlockStore::put`, so that its tracked set holds exactly that one block file, exits 1 with stderr starting `empty_home` and containing `holds no sessions` and `ship after a session has been captured`; `<tmp>/remote.git` and `<home>/.git` do not exist afterwards.

After one well-formed entry line is appended to `sessions/fixture.jsonl` directly, ship exits 1, stdout parses as `{"command": "ship", "refused": "stale_index", "sessions": [{"session": "fixture", "reason": "index_not_this_file"}]}`, `<tmp>/remote.git` and `<home>/.git` do not exist, and the SHA-256 of `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` is unchanged.

With `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` removed, ship exits 1 with stderr starting `index_missing` and containing `fixture`, `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` and `lys-home given --home`; `<tmp>/remote.git` does not exist and `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` still does not exist.

With `sessions/fixture.head` removed, ship exits 1 with stderr starting `head_missing` and containing `fixture`, `sessions/fixture.head` and `lys-home given --home`; `<tmp>/remote.git` does not exist and `sessions/fixture.head` still does not exist.

While the test process holds `Home::open(<home>)?.open_session("fixture")`, ship exits 1 with stderr starting `session_held` and containing `fixture` and `ship after that seat stops`, and not containing `ship without that session`; `<tmp>/remote.git` and `<home>/.git` do not exist.

On the fixture home above (session `fixture`, with its index and head), which the test first makes a git repository tracking `notes.txt` at the home root, ship exits 1 with stderr starting `foreign_tracked` and containing `notes.txt`, and `<tmp>/remote.git` does not exist.

Two ships to `<tmp>/remote.git` with no change between them both exit 0; the second reports `unchanged` true, `initialised` false, the first report's `commit`, and `note` equal to `the home is unchanged since <that commit>; no new commit was made`; `git --git-dir <tmp>/remote.git rev-list --count refs/lys/home` prints `1` and `git --git-dir <tmp>/remote.git rev-parse refs/lys/home` prints that commit.

A ship after one entry is appended through `Session::append` and the session dropped exits 0 with `unchanged` false and a new commit whose only parent is the first ship's commit, and the remote's `refs/lys/home` names the new commit.

A ship of a second fixture home, built separately, to the same `<tmp>/remote.git` exits 1 with stderr starting `ref_diverged` and containing `refs/lys/home`, the first home's commit, and the commit `git --git-dir <second home>/.git rev-parse refs/lys/home` prints; `git --git-dir <tmp>/remote.git rev-parse refs/lys/home` still prints the first home's commit.

Every ship in `tests/home_ship.rs`, whether it exits 0 or 1, runs through one helper, `ship_unchanged`, which takes the SHA-256 of every file of the shipped home's tracked set (R1) and the set of paths under its `sessions/`, `blocks/` and `templates/` other than `..lock` files immediately before that ship, asserts both are equal immediately after that same ship, and returns the number of files it compared; each caller asserts that number is at least 1, no other code in the file runs the `ship` subcommand, and the append through `Session::append` between two ships therefore falls outside every compared pair.

requirements.title: Fetch the shipped ref into a new home, verify it, and hang one arrival beside each session's head
requirements.spec: Add `lys-home fetch --remote <path> --home <dir>`: its arguments and run function in `crates/lys-home/src/cli_move.rs`, its enum arm in `crates/lys-home/src/cli.rs`, its logic in `crates/lys-home/src/home_move/fetch.rs`, and the removal of what it created in `crates/lys-home/src/home_move/undo.rs`. WHEN fetch runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL, before writing anything: take the remote as R3 does, refusing with the same `remote_not_local` text ship uses; refuse with `target_holds_home` when `<dir>/sessions` exists; refuse with `target_not_empty` when `<dir>` exists and holds any entry; and refuse with `HomeError::EventTooLarge` when the arrival data (R4) for the resolved remote and `refs/lys/home`, with a 40-digit commit and a 32-digit execution id, would exceed 512 bytes. THE SYSTEM SHALL then record every path it creates: `<dir>` when it did not exist, `<dir>/.git`, each file and directory the checkout writes, and each lock file opening a session creates; initialise `<dir>/.git`; fetch `refs/lys/home` from the remote into the target repository's `refs/lys/home`; write the fetched commit's tree into `<dir>` with the target repository's HEAD at that commit; and verify the home (R2, sessions, blocks and templates). IF verification gives any session a reason or names any block or template, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL print `{"command": "fetch", "refused": "verification_failed", "sessions": [{"session", "reason"}...], "bad_blocks": [<hash>...], "bad_templates": [<hash>...]}` on stdout, remove exactly the recorded paths, deepest first, check that `<dir>` is then absent when fetch created it and existing and empty when it existed before, and exit 1, appending no arrival. WHEN verification passes, THE SYSTEM SHALL, for each session in `Home::session_ids` order, open the session, append the arrival event (R4) through `Session::append_beside` with the fetched commit, the resolved remote, `refs/lys/home` and a fresh execution id from `record::fresh_id`, and release it; then stage the changed session and index files, write the tree, commit it with `git commit-tree` with the fetched commit as its only parent and the message `arrival from <remote> <ref> at <source commit>`, and set both `refs/lys/home` and the target repository's HEAD to that commit; write `<dir>/.git/info/exclude` holding exactly the line `/sessions/*..lock`, so the lock files opening a session leaves are not shown as untracked; IF appending an arrival or any step of that commit fails, THEN remove exactly the recorded paths as a failed verification does and refuse with `arrival_failed`, naming the failed step (`append` with the session, or the git subcommand) and no output of it; then print `{"command": "fetch", "report": {"commit", "remote", "ref", "sessions": [{"session", "execution"}...]}}`. Every refusal but `verification_failed` is printed on stderr with nothing on stdout and exits 1; a refusal after the first write removes the recorded paths as a failed verification does. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT move a head, SHALL NOT write a block or a template, SHALL NOT make any commit in the target's repository but the one arrival commit, SHALL NOT leave a target holding an arrival that is not committed, SHALL NOT write a home-level id file, SHALL NOT remove or change any path it did not create, SHALL NOT write anything to the remote or to the source home, and SHALL NOT put a block's bytes or an entry's data in a report or an error.
acceptance: In `tests/home_fetch.rs`, after the fixture home of R5 ships to `<tmp>/remote.git`, `fetch --remote <tmp>/remote.git --home <tmp>/target` with `<tmp>/target` absent exits 0, its report's `commit` equals the ship's, its `ref` is `refs/lys/home`, and `git -C <tmp>/target rev-parse HEAD^1` prints that commit.

For every path of the source's tracked set, the SHA-256 of the output of `git -C <tmp>/target cat-file blob <commit>:<path>` equals the SHA-256 of the source's file, and `git -C <tmp>/target ls-tree -r --name-only <commit>` lists exactly those paths, the `templates/` path included.

After fetch, `<tmp>/target/sessions/fixture.head` is byte-identical to the source's `sessions/fixture.head`, and every file under the target's `blocks/` and `templates/` is byte-identical to the source's, with the same count.

The last line of `<tmp>/target/sessions/fixture.jsonl` parses as a `custom` entry of `customType` `lys.harness_event` whose `parentId` is the id the head file names, whose `data.kind` is `arrival`, `data.detail.source_commit` the ship's commit, `data.detail.remote` the absolute path of `<tmp>/remote.git`, `data.detail.ref` `refs/lys/home`, and `data.detail.execution` 32 lowercase hex digits that occur in no file of the source home and equal the report's `execution` for `fixture`; after the arrival, the target's session verifies with no reason (R2).
The template hash every `template_render` event of the target's `fixture` session names is a file under the target's `templates/`.
After fetch, `git -C <tmp>/target status --porcelain` prints nothing.

After fetch, `git -C <tmp>/target rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD` prints the HEAD commit followed by exactly one parent, the ship's commit; `git -C <tmp>/target rev-parse refs/lys/home` prints the HEAD commit; `git -C <tmp>/target diff --name-only <ship commit> HEAD` lists exactly `sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` and `sessions/fixture.jsonl`; the bytes of `git -C <tmp>/target cat-file blob HEAD:sessions/fixture.jsonl` are the bytes of the same path at the ship's commit followed by exactly one line, the arrival line the target's file ends with, and those of `HEAD:sessions/fixture.index.jsonl` are the ship commit's index bytes followed by exactly one line; `git -C <tmp>/target log -1 --format=%B HEAD` contains the ship's commit, the absolute path of `<tmp>/remote.git` and `refs/lys/home`.

A ship from the target to `<tmp>/onward.git` exits 0 with `unchanged` true and `commit` equal to the output of `git -C <tmp>/target rev-parse HEAD`, and the last line of `git --git-dir <tmp>/onward.git cat-file blob refs/lys/home:sessions/fixture.jsonl` is an arrival whose `data.detail.execution` equals the fetch report's `execution` for `fixture`.

With a `git` script placed ahead of the real git on the PATH of the fetch process, which exits 1 when its arguments include `commit-tree` and otherwise runs the real git with the same arguments, fetch into an absent `<tmp>/nocommit` exits 1 with stderr starting `arrival_failed` and containing `commit-tree`, nothing on stdout, and `<tmp>/nocommit` does not exist afterwards; the same fetch into `<tmp>/was-empty-2`, an empty directory made beforehand, leaves it existing and holding no entry.

A fixture home with two sessions, `fixture` and `second`, shipped and fetched, reports two sessions whose `execution` values differ, and each session file's last line is an arrival carrying its own session's `execution`.

Fetching into a directory that holds `sessions/` exits 1 with stderr starting `target_holds_home`; into a directory holding one file `x.txt`, with stderr starting `target_not_empty`; in both, the directory's listing and file hashes are unchanged.

`fetch --remote https://github.com/o/r.git --home <tmp>/empty`, where `<tmp>/empty` is an empty directory made beforehand, exits 1 with stderr starting `remote_not_local` and containing `shipping off this machine waits for stage 3's encryption from the secrets step`, and `<tmp>/empty` exists afterwards and holds no entry.

After one block's bytes in a copy of the fixture home are replaced by `corrupted-block-bytes` and that copy ships to a fresh remote, fetch into an absent `<tmp>/bad` exits 1, stdout parses with `refused` `verification_failed` and `bad_blocks` equal to `[<that block's hash>]`, stdout does not contain `corrupted-block-bytes`, and `<tmp>/bad` does not exist afterwards.
The same fetch into `<tmp>/was-empty`, an empty directory made beforehand, exits 1 with the same `bad_blocks`, and `<tmp>/was-empty` exists afterwards and holds no entry.

A bare remote the test fills with plain git from a copy of the fixture home whose `sessions/fixture.jsonl` has one line appended directly, pushed to `refs/lys/home`, fetched into an absent `<tmp>/stale` exits 1 with stdout's `sessions` equal to `[{"session": "fixture", "reason": "index_not_this_file"}]`, and `<tmp>/stale` does not exist afterwards.
Fetching from a bare repository whose absolute path is 400 bytes long exits 1 with stderr containing `over the limit`, and the target does not exist afterwards.
The SHA-256 of every file under the source home's `sessions/`, `blocks/` and `templates/`, and `git --git-dir <tmp>/remote.git rev-parse refs/lys/home`, are the same before the fetch and after it.

requirements.title: Search the shipped ref for the fixture secret and render the fetched home
requirements.spec: Add `crates/lys-home/tests/home_move.rs`, run through the binary. WHEN the fixture home of R5 has been rendered with `render-launch`, shipped and fetched, with `LYS_FIXTURE_TOKEN` set to `fixture-secret-value-0001` in the environment of every lys-home process the test runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL hold no object reachable from the shipped ref whose bytes contain that value, and a `render-launch` of the target's session SHALL record the same `session_head` as a `render-launch` of the source's session. The search SHALL read every object `git rev-list --objects refs/lys/home` lists, each through `git cat-file`, and SHALL count the objects it read. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT run the printed launch line in a test (ADR-007), and SHALL NOT render the source for the comparison before the source's byte-identity is asserted.
acceptance: The search reads exactly as many objects as the tracked set's paths plus the fetched tree's directories, its root included, plus 1 commit, and finds `fixture-secret-value-0001` 0 times.
The same search over a scratch bare repository holding one blob `token=fixture-secret-value-0001` finds it exactly 1 time.

After the source's tracked files are asserted byte-identical, `render-launch` of session `fixture` on the target and on the source, each into its own empty out directory with the same `--uuid`, `--cwd`, `--model` and `--version`, report equal `session_head` values, and the target's report's launch line names `<target out>/<uuid>.jsonl` after `--resume`.

requirements.title: Document the arrival, the tracked set, ship and fetch
requirements.spec: Structural: `docs/design/home/RECORD.md` gains the `arrival` kind beside the six harness_event kinds, with its four detail fields, that it hangs beside the head as `template_render` does and moves no head, and that it is one per arriving session with its own execution id; and a section stating that a home directory is a git repository tracking exactly the set R1 enumerates, on the fixed ref `refs/lys/home`, and that fetch commits the arrival entries as one commit whose parent is the fetched commit, so a later ship from the target carries them. `crates/lys-home/README.md` gains `ship` and `fetch` with their arguments, what each report carries, every refusal name (`remote_not_local`, `remote_not_bare`, `empty_home`, `session_held`, `index_missing`, `head_missing`, `stale_index`, `foreign_tracked`, `ref_diverged`, `target_holds_home`, `target_not_empty`, `verification_failed`, `arrival_failed`, `git_failed`), and the sentence that no credential lys-home holds is ever written into the home, that ship does not scan for secrets because blocks hold imported tool results verbatim and a template's env and mcp slots are free strings, and that this is why ship takes only a path on this machine. The module docs at the top of `crates/lys-home/src/cli.rs` list `ship` and `fetch`. The cluster's rendered markdown, `docs/design/home/DESIGN.md`, `CHECKLIST.md`, `USER-STORIES.md` and `briefs/HOME-019.md`, is regenerated with `python3 scripts/design/render-cluster.py docs/design/home` from the cluster's JSON and never edited by hand. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT change what either document says of the six existing kinds, lys.given, lanterns or forks, SHALL NOT claim that ship keeps every secret out of a home, and SHALL NOT edit a rendered markdown file by hand.
acceptance: RECORD.md names `arrival` and, in the arrival's description, `source_commit`, `remote`, `ref` and `execution`.

RECORD.md lists `sessions/<id>.jsonl`, `sessions/<id>.index.jsonl`, `sessions/<id>.head`, `blocks/<hh>/<hash>` and `templates/<hh>/<hash>` as the tracked set and names `sessions/<id>..lock` as never tracked.
Each of the fourteen refusal names above occurs in `crates/lys-home/README.md`.
`crates/lys-home/README.md` contains `no credential lys-home holds is ever written into the home`, `verbatim` and `free strings`.
From the repository root, `sh scripts/design/gate.sh` exits 0.

requirements.title: Measure the move and the resume of the fetched home on Claude Code 2.1.283
requirements.spec: Structural: `docs/design/home/PROOF-MOVE.md` records, as hashes, counts, paths, commands, versions and exit codes only: the Claude Code version `claude --version` prints where the proof runs, which is 2.1.283; a fixture home with a synthetic session built as R5 builds it, rendered once with `render-launch`; the ship command, its report and the remote's ref; the SHA-256 of every tracked file of the source before the ship and after the fetch; the fetch command and its report; the target's head file hash beside the source's, and the arrival's execution id; the secret search's object count and match count; `render-launch` run on the target and its report's `session_head` beside a source render's; the printed launch line run by hand, never by lys-home, with `-p` and one question asking for the last word of the session's final assistant message; the run's exit code; the SHA-256 of the reply, trimmed of surrounding whitespace, stripped of one trailing full stop and lowercased, beside the SHA-256 of the expected word normalised the same way; and `lys-home resume-check` on the continuation file, with its counts. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write a line of the session's text, the question's or the reply's text, a credential or a handle into the proof, and SHALL NOT record a version other than the one `claude --version` printed in the run.
acceptance: PROOF-MOVE.md names Claude Code `2.1.283` as the version the resume ran on and the version `claude --version` printed in the run it records.
The recorded tracked-file hashes of the source before the ship equal the recorded hashes after the fetch.
The recorded head file hash of the target equals the source's, and the recorded `session_head` of the target's render equals the source's.
The recorded secret search reads more than 0 objects and finds 0 matches.
The recorded launch run exits 0, the SHA-256 of its normalised reply equals the SHA-256 of the normalised expected word, and `resume-check` reports 0 repeated tool uses.
PROOF-MOVE.md contains none of the fixture session's text parts, compared line by line after trimming, and neither the question's text nor `fixture-secret-value-0001`.

boundaries: SHALL NOT take a remote that is not a path on this machine: no ssh remote to any host, no https, git or file URL, no hosted service, and no estate-hosts file, ssh configuration or host list read or written.
SHALL NOT encrypt a home, ship it to a second machine, or grant anyone read authority over it; those are stage 3's second block and the secrets and directory boards' cards.
SHALL NOT change docs/design/identity/CONTEXT-ROADMAP-2026-09-22.md or the home design's non-goal on encryption at rest and moving a home between devices.
SHALL NOT force-push, overwrite a remote ref that is not an ancestor of the commit being pushed, or write any file of the source home's tracked set.
SHALL NOT track or push a lock file, a temporary, a file at the home root or any file outside the tracked set, and SHALL NOT write a credential lys-home holds into the home.
SHALL NOT scan the home for secrets or claim that ship keeps every secret out of a home.
SHALL NOT add a flag or any other way for ship to leave a session out.

SHALL NOT rebuild or write an index or a head file during ship, or move a session's head, write a block or a template, or make any commit in the target's repository during fetch but the one arrival commit whose parent is the fetched commit.
SHALL NOT change the six existing harness_event kinds, the lys.given, lantern and fork entries, the render's derived uuid scheme (ADR-016), or add a field to Pi's grammar.
SHALL NOT run the launch line; render-launch prints it and the proof runs it by hand (ADR-007).
SHALL NOT add a dependency or a git crate; git runs as the binary on PATH.
SHALL NOT support a harness other than Claude Code.
SHALL NOT put transcript content, an entry's data or a block's bytes in a report, an error, a log line, a test name or a proof document.
SHALL NOT let a test reach the network: every remote in a test is a path in a temporary directory.
verification: From the repository root: `sh scripts/design/gate.sh` exits 0.

From the repository root: `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` and `cargo doc --no-deps` exit 0.

Every new source file under `crates/lys-home/src` has at most 500 lines of code, counted without comments and blank lines; `record/mod.rs` gains only `pub mod` and test-module lines, and `home_move/mod.rs` holds only `pub mod` lines and module docs.
`cargo test -p lys-home --all-features --test home_ship --test home_fetch --test home_move` passes and its output lists every test named in R5, R6 and R7.
Read PROOF-MOVE.md against R9's acceptance: every figure is a hash, a count, a path, a command, a version or an exit code.
